# NEAR: three layers, one token

> **NEAR isn't just an L1 anymore. It's a three-layer business, and the token is only beginning to capture that value.**

An investment thesis for the NEAR HACKATHON (Investment Thesis track), with data as of {asof}. Every chart, with the query behind it, is on the [dashboard](DASHBOARD.md). How each number is computed is in [METHODS.md](METHODS.md). This is research, not investment advice.

The claim is the line above. The evidence for it runs through the next four sections, the evidence against it is under [Risks and considerations](#risks-and-considerations), and the results that would change our mind are in [the last table](#what-would-change-our-mind).

## Key points

{key_points}

## The problem NEAR solves

Crypto is spread across hundreds of blockchains, each with its own assets and apps. Moving money between them usually takes several steps, a bridge, and a fee at each one. AI has a different problem: a few companies run the most capable models, and they see everything people send them.

NEAR has built a product for each problem. NEAR Intents turns a swap between any two chains into one step. NEAR AI runs AI models on hardware that keeps prompts private, even from NEAR AI. Both tie back to the NEAR token.

NEAR is still mostly judged as a base-layer blockchain (an L1), and on those numbers it looks like a network in decline: L1 transactions fell from {l1_tx_first} a day in {l1_tx_first_month} to {l1_tx_last} in {l1_tx_last_month}. That view misses where the business went.

## NEAR's three layers

NEAR now works as three businesses, each built on the one below it.

**NEAR L1, the base chain.** The blockchain itself: accounts, smart contracts and payments, at an average fee of about {l1_fee} a transaction. Its own traffic has fallen, but more of what remains is Intents. In {c2_month}, {c2_share} of L1 transactions went to the Intents contract, against {c2_share_yago} a year earlier.

**NEAR Intents, cross-chain swaps.** A user says what they have and what they want, competing market makers fill the order, and NEAR settles the result. In {m}, Intents handled {int_vol} of swaps, {int_vol_x} its level a year earlier. On 1Click, the Intents channel with public swap-by-swap data, {int_users} users swapped through {int_apps} apps, starting from {int_chains} chains.

**NEAR AI, private AI.** NEAR AI Cloud runs open AI models inside secure hardware, so no one, not even NEAR AI, can read the prompts. Customers pay per use, or stake NEAR and receive AI credits. It is the newest layer. On OpenRouter, a marketplace for AI models, it served {ai_last} tokens (units of text) in the week to {ai_last_week}, {ai_x} its first full week. Brave's AI assistant has run on it since {brave_date}.

The layers are built to feed each other. AI agents need to pay and trade across chains, which is what Intents does, and every Intents swap settles on the L1.

The money has already moved. Intents produced {c1_share3} of NEAR's protocol revenue over {c1_last3}, against {c1_share3_yago} a year earlier.

![NEAR protocol revenue by source, monthly](site/charts/c1-revenue.svg)

## Why the NEAR token has value

The token gains when NEAR is taken out of circulation, or locked up, faster than new NEAR is issued. Four mechanisms do that, and each one started or changed in the last {mech_months} months.

- **Fees and burns.** Every L1 transaction pays a fee in NEAR. {gas_txt}
- **Buybacks.** NEAR keeps a share of the fees on Intents swaps. Since {bb_date}, that share buys NEAR on the market.
- **Staking.** NEAR is staked to secure the chain. Since {ai_open}, holders can also stake with NEAR AI and receive AI credits. The NEAR stays locked while it is staked.
- **Less new supply.** On {infl_date}, NEAR cut its cap on new issuance from {infl_from} to {infl_to} a year. A second cut, HSP-029, passed on {hsp_passed} and would lower it to {hsp_target} by {hsp_end}.

![Follow the money: what each layer earned, and what reached the token](site/charts/money-flow.svg)

{flow_caption}

**How much it adds up to.** Burns and buybacks offset {c6_ratio} of the new NEAR issued in {c6_q}, against {c6_ratio_yago} a year earlier. Counting NEAR newly staked with NEAR AI, the figure reached {incl_ai}. Most new NEAR is still not offset, which is why we say the token is only beginning to capture the value.

![Share of new NEAR offset by burns and buybacks, monthly](site/charts/c6-ratio.svg)

**Where it could go.** {outlook} These are projections from a short history, not forecasts. The assumptions are in [METHODS.md](METHODS.md#scenarios).

## NEAR in context

Intents is growing faster than its market. Among the venues that swap native assets between chains (Intents, THORChain, Chainflip and Maya), its share of volume rose from {c4_yago} to {c4_share} over the year to {c4_last}. Its volume grew {c4_growth} in that time, while total DEX volume {c4_dex_move}.

{context_table}

> **Brave.** Brave's browser has over {brave_mau} monthly users. Since {brave_date}, its AI assistant Leo offers {brave_model} running on NEAR AI Cloud, so Leo users who pick that model get private AI they can verify. {customers}

**Where NEAR stands today.** It is worth being direct about this. Intents is a working, growing business, and it already pays for buybacks. NEAR AI is early: it publishes no revenue, and we estimate its OpenRouter sales at about {ai_annual} a year. The token is earliest of all, because the mechanisms that send value to it have only just been switched on. The business has already moved beyond the L1 and the token has barely begun to reflect it, which is why our view is long-term bullish.

## Risks and considerations

This section is the evidence against the thesis, in one place.

{risks}

**What we couldn't measure.** NEAR AI publishes neither revenue nor total usage, so we see only its OpenRouter traffic and on-chain staking. Our user counts cover the 1Click channel only, about {oneclick_share} of Intents volume in {c3_month}. Market share is against a peer set, not the whole cross-chain market. The full list is in [METHODS.md](METHODS.md#what-we-couldnt-compute).
